title: Model Versioning and A/B Testing
summary: Version the complete inference behavior and compare releases through stable assignment, meaningful outcome measures, and reversible promotion.
overview: Model versioning identifies the full behavior-producing bundle: model weights or provider revision, tokenizer, prompt, tools, retrieval configuration, adapter, and runtime settings. A model name alone is insufficient when several surrounding components change. Reproducible evaluation requires knowing exactly which bundle produced each outcome.

A/B testing assigns comparable traffic to alternative bundles to estimate differences in task outcomes. Stable user or workflow assignment avoids mixing behaviors within one experience. Shadow evaluation sends copies for observation without allowing the shadow path to perform external effects. Canary rollout primarily limits operational exposure; it is not automatically a statistically valid experiment.

production.poc: A prototype compares candidate and baseline on the same held-out task set with deterministic scoring where possible.
production.production: Production uses immutable bundle IDs, stable assignment, predefined metrics, and an immediate rollback route.
production.scale: Enterprise scale monitors subgroup regressions, experiment interactions, delayed outcomes, and data-policy eligibility before promoting a candidate.

components.name: Behavior registry
components.role: Stores immutable model and surrounding configuration lineage.

components.name: Assignment service
components.role: Routes a stable eligible cohort to baseline or candidate.

components.name: Outcome collector
components.role: Associates task quality, latency, cost, and failure evidence with the assigned bundle.

components.name: Evaluation gate
components.role: Applies predefined acceptance criteria and checks important slices.

components.name: Release controller
components.role: Promotes or rolls back traffic without losing in-flight workflow identity.

flow.title: Register the complete bundle
flow.description: Pin the model, prompts, tools, retrieval, and runtime configuration.

flow.title: Define the comparison
flow.description: Choose task metrics, guardrails, eligible traffic, and assignment unit before exposure.

flow.title: Run offline and shadow checks
flow.description: Reject obvious regressions before live impact and suppress shadow side effects.

flow.title: Assign live cohorts
flow.description: Keep a user or workflow on a stable version according to the experiment design.

flow.title: Analyze outcomes
flow.description: Compare quality, cost, latency, and subgroup behavior while accounting for incomplete observations.

flow.title: Promote or revert
flow.description: Record the decision and retain the prior bundle and routing configuration for recovery.

useCase.title: Comparing resume-summary models
useCase.situation: An internal assistant prepares factual summaries of candidate documents for recruiters.
useCase.problem: A new model writes more concise summaries but may omit important experience details.
useCase.requirement: Compare completeness and factual support while preserving a consistent recruiter workflow.
useCase.architecture: A behavior registry and stable session assignment route eligible tasks to two evaluated bundles.
runtime: Reviewers score source-supported field coverage without seeing the bundle identity.
The analysis checks omission rates by document format and language before promotion.
useCase.failure: If one language slice regresses despite a better overall score, the candidate is withheld or restricted to validated traffic.
useCase.impact: Measure accepted summary quality, omissions, latency, and cost; user clicks alone can reflect presentation preference rather than factual correctness.

tradeoffs.cost: May require larger cohorts for balanced comparisons.

tradeoffs.benefit: Tests behavior without direct user impact.
tradeoffs.cost: Adds inference cost and must suppress tool effects.
Requires disciplined configuration and artifact management.

failures.detection: Observed improvement cannot be attributed clearly.
failures.recovery: Use a documented bundle comparison or isolate changes intentionally.

failures.scenario: Shadow path executes a real tool
failures.detection: Duplicate side effects appear during evaluation.
failures.recovery: Use read-only fixtures or block shadow effect dispatch.

mistakes.mistake: Using mutable model aliases as versions
mistakes.fix: Record resolved provider or artifact identity.
Inspect critical language, task, and tenant slices.

mistakes.mistake: Calling a small canary a conclusive A/B test
mistakes.fix: Separate exposure control from statistical inference.

whenToUse: Use for model, prompt, adapter, or retrieval releases.
Use when quality and cost tradeoffs need real workload evidence.
Use when rollback must reproduce the previous behavior.
whenNotToUse: Avoid experiments without reliable task outcomes.
Do not expose ineligible sensitive data to candidate providers.
